diffs.diff: illuminance_lux_10000lux_range: datasheet reading gives 0.15259 per count, the part's model has 1, 1, 1
diffs.evidence: The two readings measure different quantities. The model's three measures (registers 0x09, 0x0B, 0x0D) are the raw green/red/blue ADC values in 'counts' with scale 1; the driver returns them unchanged. The datasheet (FN8424.2) states 'DFS Full Scale ADC Code: ADC 16 bits 65535 Counts', so scale 1 count per count is right. The second reading's 0.15259 is just 10,000 lux / 65,536, the per-count resolution from the front-page line 'Range 1 = 0.152 lux to 10,000 lux'. It is not a conversion from a channel to lux. The datasheet's 'Calculating Lux' section gives 'Ev = Y = ( CYRxRed + CYGxGreen + CYBxBlue )xRange (EQ. 2)', and the CY coefficients have to be calibrated for each design. The model's build notes say this ('converting to lux ... needs coefficients calibrated for your enclosure (datasheet equation 2)'). Multiplying one channel by 0.15259 would give a wrong lux value, so the model's raw-count scale stays.
